chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥusayn, from Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Muskān, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام led us in salat (prayer).
Then he recited for us: al-Ḍuḥā and Alam Nashraḥ.

Because in this report it is not stated whether he recited them in one rakʿah or in two rakʿahs. So when this very narrator himself has narrated this very ruling itself and clarified that he recited them in a single rakʿah, then interpreting this unrestricted narration in a way that accords with that is more appropriate, and that does not contradict it.

key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ الْمُطْلَقَةِ: a narration stated without specifying a restricting detail
key_terms.الْحُكْمَ: the legal ruling conveyed by the report
key_terms.بِالضُّحَى: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā as recited in salat (prayer)
key_terms.وَأَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ: Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ paired in recitation with al-Ḍuḥā

ai.seo_question: Can Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā and Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ be recited together in one rakʿah of the obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling on joining two surahs in the obligatory salat (prayer), specifically Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā and Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ. The accompanying explanation clarifies that this narration is to be understood in light of another report from the same narrator stating that both were recited in a single rakʿah, making it relevant to legal reasoning about recitation in the farīḍah.
